newsitem.title: USA: PSE&G settles Salem suits, to restate Q1.
newsitem.headline: PSE&G settles Salem suits, to restate Q1.

text.p: Public Service Electric and Gas Co said Monday it has settled the lawsuit brought by Salem co-owners PECO Energy Co and Delmarva Power & Light Co.

Under the settlement, the Public Service Enterprise Group Inc subsidiary will pay $82 million to the two co-owners. It said this will result in an after-tax charge of $53.3 million, or $0.23 per share, against the company's previously reported first quarter results, which will be restated.
As a result of the restatement, Enterprise said, its first quarter earnings were cut to $139.5 million or $0.60 a share.
This compares with the $194.1 million, or $0.79 per share, the company earned in the first quarter of 1996.
On April 15, the company reported first quarter 1997 earnings of $192.8 million, or $0.83 per share.

Also under the settlement, PSE&G said, it would be obligated to pay $1.4 million for each reactor month the outage continued beyond an aggregate outage of 64 reactor months up to a maximum payment of $17 million.
The Salem station has been out of service for 47 reactor months through April 30 and the company does not expect to be required to make any payments under this provision, it said.
Salem Unit 2 is expected to return to service early in the third quarter and Salem Unit 1 is expected to resume operation late this year, it noted.
The settlement also sets operating standards through December 31, 2011, for Salem and a similar standard for the Peach Bottom nuclear station operated by PECO, PSE&G said.

Salem units 1 and 2 have 1,106 megawatts of capacity each, while Peach Bottom 2 and 3 have 1,100 megawatts each. PECO and PSE&G have a 42.5 percent interest in all four while Delmarva Power and Atlantic Energy Inc own 7.5 percent each.

Under the performance standards, the operater would be required to make payments to the non-operating owners if the three-year capacity factor determined annually for either station fell below 40 percent, subject to a maximum of $25 million per year, PSE&G said.
The initial three year period begins on January 1, 1998.
The parties further agreed to forego litigation in the future, except for limited cases in which the operator would be responsible for no more than $5 million per year.
The settlement of the suit, which was filed March 6, 1996, precludes a trial that was to begin on May 20 in the U.S. District Court in Philadelphia, PSE&G said.
